title: Backcasting from 'Compute Thresholds Track Real Risk': Stress-Testing the 1e25 FLOP Systemic-Risk Trigger

original_idea.body:
# Backcasting from 'Compute Thresholds Track Real Risk': Stress-Testing the 1e25 FLOP Systemic-Risk Trigger

**Problem:** A success state where compute thresholds (e.g., EU AI Act's 1e25 FLOP) correctly identify systemic-risk models requires that the threshold correlate with actual dangerous capability. With efficiency gains (~40%/year more compute-per-dollar), a fixed FLOP line may misclassify models, letting capable-but-efficient models slip below it.

**Direction:** Using Epoch AI's public model database (3200+ models with compute estimates) plus public benchmark scores (e.g., MMLU/GPQA leaderboards), build a simple regression/scatter analysis of training-FLOP vs measured capability over time. Quantify how the FLOP-to-capability mapping drifts with algorithmic efficiency, and estimate how many models cross capability bars while sitting below 1e25 FLOP. Produce a 'threshold drift' visualization.

**Why it matters:** Backcasting from 'thresholds gate the right models' reveals the precondition that compute must proxy capability stably — which efficiency progress erodes. A concrete drift analysis warns regulators that static FLOP thresholds decay, informing compute-governance design. Uses only Epoch's open data; no training, strong outsider counterfactual.

**Relevant context:** Epoch AI: frontier compute grows 4-5x/yr, compute-per-dollar +40%/yr; EU AI Act systemic-risk threshold = 1e25 FLOP. Open Problems in Technical AI Governance treats compute as a blunt but key lever; Lennart Heim's compute-governance work.
